summary:
Workplace Insight reports that entries are open for the 2027 Design Guild Mark Awards, run by The Furniture Makers' Company. The not-for-profit recognition programme, established in 2008, raises the profile of British industrial design. Entries are invited in three categories: Furniture, Lighting and Interior Design Elements, with a final deadline of 29 January 2027 via designguildmark.org.uk.

Eligibility is broad. Any project may be entered, from a single standout product to a full collection, provided it is in production and was designed for and made through an industrial design process. Domestic, office, hospitality, educational and corporate work is welcome, indoors or out. The award is open to British designers working in the UK or abroad, and to designers with UK-based practices.

The programme differs from conventional competitions in that applicants present to a panel of independent expert judges, and every design meeting the standard earns a Mark rather than competing for a single winning spot. Entries are assessed against five criteria: Innovation (new, original thinking and problem solving), Function (fit for purpose, intuitive, beneficial to the user), Form (aesthetics, build quality, innovative materials or processes), Brand (strengthening market position or competitive edge), and Environment (sustainable and circular practice, longevity of appeal and use).

Recipients in each category are put forward for the Jonathan Hindle Prize for Excellence.

Alex Crofts, Chairman of the Design Guild Mark and CEO of Crofts & Assinder Ltd, said the design sector is a major contributor to the UK economy and that the Mark promotes UK design as a leading global creative force, open to seasoned designers and rising talent alike. Amy Heffernan, formerly Interiors Director at Wallpaper* and a contributor to Elle Decoration, has joined the Design Guild Mark committee.

The main image features a past winner, the Thinking Quietly booth designed by Jones and Partners for Thinking Works, awarded in 2018.
